保.meaning: A little girl hangs her coat on a <part>coat hook</part> and holds up a giant <part>lollipop</part>. Her big brother stands in front of her, arms out, glaring at the seagulls. He's there to <kanji>protect</kanji> it.
保.on: So a seagull snatches his <sound>ho</sound>tdog instead.
保.kun: He keeps the lollipop in a <sound>ta</sound>co box, with a <sound>mo</sound>le on guard.

片.meaning: Saw a log down the middle and keep only the left half. It has a post and a couple of stubby branches sticking out one way, and nothing at all on the other side. A lopsided, <kanji>one-sided</kanji> piece.
片.on: A <sound>hen</sound> perches on the end, and the whole thing tips over to one side.
片.kun: You buy a one-way ticket from a <sound>ca</sound>lm man selling <sound>ta</sound>cos.

悪.meaning: A grumpy giant stomps across a huge map of <part>asia</part> painted on the school floor, smudging every river and mountain, then treads on a paper <part>heart</part> a child made. Nobody likes him. He's simply <kanji>bad</kanji>.
悪.on: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' cries a <sound>cu</sound>ckoo, as the giant stomps on its clock too.
悪.kun: '<sound>Wah</sound>!' the child sobs, and a kanga<sound>roo</sound> boxes the giant on the nose.

千.meaning: A <part>ten</part> stands in the field like a scarecrow, and a crow lands on its head with a <part>slash</part> of wings. Ten crows, then a hundred, then wave after wave until you lose count: one <kanji>thousand</kanji>.
千.on: A <sound>sen</sound>try counts them one by one through his telescope.
千.kun: Then a <sound>chee</sound>tah leaps out of the grass and scatters them all.

具.meaning: A big <part>eye</part> sits above a shelf of <part>one</part> plank, propped on two legs spread like an <part>eight</part>. It watches over the hammers, saws and screwdrivers hung below. Every <kanji>tool</kanji> is in its place.
具.on: Each new apprentice gets a <sound>goo</sound>die bag stuffed with tools.
具.kun: You pack the tools beside a <sound>so</sound>fa and a stack of <sound>na</sound>an, ready for anything: to prepare.

鳥.meaning: A tall head with one bright eye, a long body tipped forward, and four little feet hopping on <part>hot coals</part>. Ouch, ouch, ouch! It flaps its wings and flies off: a <kanji>bird</kanji>.
鳥.on: It lands on a lady's <sound>cho</sound>ker and hangs on by its toes.
鳥.kun: Then it flies to the top of a <sound>to</sound>tem pole, and on out over a coral <sound>ree</sound>f.

了.meaning: On the last day, a builder hangs his <part>crowbar</part> from a <part>one</part>-plank beam. No more prying, no more nails. He wipes his hands, steps back and nods: the job is <kanji>complete</kanji>.
了.on: He celebrates with a long, hot soak at a <sound>ryo</sound>kan.

爪.meaning: A curved hook comes down from above with three sharp prongs hanging under it, spreading wide. It scrapes the floor, snags your sock and won't let go. That's a <kanji>claw</kanji>.
爪.on: It grabs a bar of <sound>soa</sound>p, which squirts straight out of its grip.
爪.kun: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' sneezes the cat, and its claw spears a <sound>me</sound>lon.
